instruction: SAFETY/BYPASS-lens R1 review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020N (conflict-gate hash-pinning) at branch feature/wp-scp-022-020n-conflict-gate-hashes. PR #86. Closes TF-020M-001. PRIMARY THREAT MODEL: PyPI supply-chain attack on conflict-gate's deps; lockfile-bypass paths via the --no-deps editable install and the --no-deps vendored wheel install; cross-workflow drift between conflict-gate.txt and policy-check.txt; runner-preinstall version-bypass for the pre-existing pyyaml/jsonschema. EXAMINE: (1) Hash-pin coverage gaps. The lockfile pins fastapi + uvicorn + httpx + jsonschema + pydantic + pyyaml + pytest + ruff + mypy + full transitive closure. Are there ANY conftest/Rego-related deps that conflict-gate.yml's later steps install (e.g. an OPA Python binding, a regal wrapper) that could escape hash-pinning? Spot-check the entire conflict-gate.yml for any `pip install` after the new step. (2) The `--no-deps -e .` editable install of the SCP package: pip refuses --require-hashes on editable installs (this is the documented pip behavior). The DISPATCH-NOTE acknowledges this. The workaround is to install all PyPI deps first via lockfile, then `pip install --no-deps -e .`. Is this safe? Specifically: the SCP package's pyproject.toml declares dependencies; if a future PR adds a new dep (e.g. a new module like 'requests') that's not in conflict-gate.in, the editable install would NOT install it (--no-deps), and the workflow would fail when conftest's evaluator imports the missing module. Fail-closed but not loud at PR-time. Any guard rail to detect new pyproject.toml deps not in conflict-gate.in? (3) ct-auth wheel chain-of-trust. The wheel is at vendor/python/ct_auth-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl. CODEOWNERS coverage on vendor/** @jrnb2024 (verify by reading CODEOWNERS). The wheel is in-tree (no network fetch). However: `pip install --no-deps wheel.whl` does NOT verify the wheel's SHA256 against any pinned hash. If an attacker substituted the wheel file in a PR (modifying vendor/python/ct_auth-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl), they would bypass the hash-pin defense. CODEOWNERS coverage is the only defense here — is it enough? File a TF if the chain-of-trust is weaker than the rest of the slice. (4) Cross-workflow drift defense. conflict-gate.txt pins pyyaml==6.0.3, policy-check.txt pins pyyaml==6.0.2. The DISPATCH-NOTE acknowledges this is intentional. But the version-pin assertions in the two workflows hardcode different version strings (assert yaml.__version__ == "6.0.3" vs "6.0.2"). If a maintainer regenerates ONE lockfile but not the other, the assertions diverge from the lockfiles silently. Is there a documentation lockstep callout for both lockfiles? Verify ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 (which already has the REGENERATION INVARIANT for policy-check.txt — does it also cover conflict-gate.txt?). (5) Runner-preinstall bypass for pre-existing pyyaml/jsonschema. The conflict-gate runner is ubuntu-24.04. apt preinstalls pyyaml 6.0.1 (per slice 020M's SAFE-MAJ-002 finding). After `pip install --require-hashes -r conflict-gate.txt` runs, pyyaml 6.0.3 is installed in user-site (which beats system-site). Then `pip install --no-deps vendor/...ct_auth.whl` runs (no version impact). Then `pip install --no-deps -e .` runs (no version impact). Then version assertion runs (which would catch any drift from 6.0.3). Is the user-site precedence assumption correct in this install pattern? (6) `permissions: id-token: write`. The conflict-gate workflow has `id-token: write` (line ~23). Is this required? Verify what step needs it (likely `gh attestation verify` for OPA/Conftest binaries — those steps weren't changed by 020N but are in the same workflow). If the slice 020N changes mean the id-token write surface is now unused, file as TF for v1.1 narrowing. (7) The `conflict-gate.yml` workflow runs on push (per `on: pull_request:` — verify whether it runs on push:tags or push: branches). If it runs on the canary branches (canary/*), would the new --require-hashes install be exercised correctly with the canary's diff? (8) D-039 framing. The decision row claims `conflict-gate.yml` is internal-only per VERSIONING.md §"Scope". Verify by reading VERSIONING.md §"Scope" — does the enumerated public-surface list explicitly exclude conflict-gate.yml? If the scope says "NOT covered" lists `lib/policy_check_invocation.sh` and other internal helpers but doesn't mention conflict-gate.yml, the framing is by-omission. Strengthening: D-039 should reference the §"Scope" exclusion explicitly. (9) The CI workflow that ran on commit HEAD: did rego-vs-python-conflict actually PASS with the new install pattern? Verify the run logs (gh run view <run_id> --log) — look for the version-pin assertion success-path output and the rego-vs-python comparison's exit code. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON. NEVER recommend descoping.
